stories.headline: Microsoft-G42 $1B Kenya Data Center Stalled by Payment-Guarantee Dispute, Not Just Power

key_facts.fact: A major Microsoft-G42 data center site in East Africa has been delayed after the Kenyan government couldn't commit to annual capacity payments at the level Microsoft requested, breaking down the talks, Bloomberg reported on May 10.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft and its partner, Abu Dhabi-based tech conglomerate G42, had asked the government to commit to paying for a certain amount of capacity annually... When the government couldn't provide the guarantees at the level Microsoft requested, the talks broke down.

key_facts.fact: The $1 billion geothermal-powered facility near Olkaria, planned for ~100 km northwest of Nairobi, was announced during President Ruto's May 2024 visit to Washington with an original May 2026 target for phase-one operation.
key_facts.excerpt: Ruto had announced plans for the huge facility during a state visit to Washington in May 2024... it would run on geothermal power... once-hyped project had stalled.

key_facts.fact: President Ruto said the facility would have required a third of Kenya's ~3,000 MW installed capacity, telling grassroots leaders: 'To switch on that one data center, we would need to shut off power for half the country.'
key_facts.excerpt: Ruto, speaking to grassroots leaders in Nairobi last week, said Kenya was forced to reconsider the plans after learning that it would require a third of the country's total installed capacity of around 3,000 megawatts. 'To switch on that one data center, we would need to shut off power for half the country.'

key_facts.fact: Phase one was a 100 MW build, well within Olkaria's roughly 950 MW geothermal capacity, suggesting the binding obstacle was risk allocation on a multi-year dollar-denominated capacity guarantee rather than grid limits.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase one was 100 MW, and Olkaria's geothermal complex generates roughly 950 MW. Phase one was always within reach... The binding question on phase one was never really the power. It was who carried the risk if East African demand for Azure capacity took longer to materialise.

key_facts.fact: Officials said the project has not been cancelled, with ongoing discussions on restructuring power capacity and financing arrangements.
key_facts.excerpt: Despite the delay, officials familiar with the talks said the project has not been cancelled, and discussions are ongoing on restructuring the deal, including power capacity and financing arrangements.

stories.headline: SoftBank Launches GWh-Scale Battery Business in Japan for AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: SoftBank Corp. announced a Japan-based battery business to support electricity demand from AI adoption, with mass production at gigawatt-hour-per-year scale targeted around fiscal 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: At the GX Factory, SoftBank plans to begin manufacturing battery cells and energy storage systems from the fiscal year ending March 31, 2028 (FY2027), with the aim of achieving mass production on a gigawatt-hour (GWh)-per-year scale by around FY2028.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank is partnering with South Korea's Cosmos Lab and DeltaX to enable mass production from the fiscal year starting in April 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank Corp. will partner with South Korea's Cosmos Lab and DeltaX to enable mass production from the fiscal year starting next April, the company said in a statement Monday. The aim is to output energy storage systems at a scale of one gigawatt-hour per year.

key_facts.fact: The plant will sit at the former Sharp Corporation LCD factory site in Sakai, Osaka, and feed the Osaka Sakai AI Data Center SoftBank is developing there.
key_facts.excerpt: SoftBank will utilize the AI Data Center it is developing on the former Sharp Corporation factory site in Sakai City, Osaka Prefecture (the 'Osaka Sakai AI Data Center') as a core hub to establish its AX Factory and the GX Factory.

key_facts.fact: SoftBank aims for annual revenue of over 100 billion yen (about $636 million) for its domestic battery business by fiscal 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The company aims to generate an annual revenue of over ¥100 billion ($636 million) through its new battery business by fiscal 2030.

key_facts.fact: Cosmos Lab is developing zinc-halide batteries, using water as electrolyte instead of rare metals such as lithium and cobalt.
key_facts.excerpt: Cosmos Lab has been developing 'zinc halide batteries' based on zinc, instead of rare metals such as lithium or cobalt that conventional batteries have relied on. The startup has also drawn attention in Korea for using water, which poses no fire risk, as its electrolyte.

stories.headline: TrendForce: AI Demand Drives 3nm and 2.5D Packaging Into Critical Shortage

key_facts.fact: TrendForce says surging AI demand has tightened 3nm-2nm wafer and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging into capacity bottlenecks, with TSMC's 3nm capacity becoming a 'scarce resource fiercely contested by global tech giants.'
key_facts.excerpt: The surging AI demand is creating capacity bottlenecks in 3nm–2 nm wafers and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging, according to TrendForce... 3nm advanced process capacity—currently dominated by TSMC—has become even more constrained, turning into a scarce resource fiercely contested by global tech giants.

key_facts.fact: TSMC's CoWoS advanced packaging has remained in short supply since 2023; TrendForce expects severe 2.5D packaging tightness to ease only slightly by 2027, aided by TSMC's plan to expand CoWoS capacity by over 60% by that year.
key_facts.excerpt: CoWoS has remained in short supply since 2023, prompting customers to seek alternative capacity sources... TrendForce expects that the severe shortage in global 2.5D packaging capacity will begin to ease slightly by 2027, aided by order spillover and TSMC's plan to expand CoWoS capacity by over 60% by 2027.

key_facts.fact: AI compute chips are migrating from 4nm to 3nm in late 2025 and 2026 while smartphones and PCs have yet to shift en masse to 2nm, concentrating high-performance demand on 3nm.
key_facts.excerpt: AI compute chips are rapidly transitioning from 4nm to 3nm between late 2025 and 2026. At the same time, high-end smartphone and PC processors have yet to migrate en masse to the next-generation 2nm node, resulting in a short-term concentration of high-performance demand on 3nm.

key_facts.fact: Samsung and Intel remain behind TSMC in 3nm progress, producing a 'temporary single-supplier dynamic dominated by TSMC,' with global 3nm capacity expected to surpass 5/4nm by year-end 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung and Intel remain behind TSMC in 3 nm foundry progress... this has led to a temporary single-supplier dynamic dominated by TSMC... global 3nm capacity is expected to surpass 5/4nm by the end of 2026 and become the second-largest process node after 28nm by 2027.

key_facts.fact: Alternative packaging technologies like Intel's EMIB and FOEB are gaining traction, while SPIL and Amkor have benefited from CoWoS shortages.
key_facts.excerpt: Providers such as SPIL and Amkor have benefited from this, and alternative technologies like EMIB and FOEB are also gaining traction, with Intel leveraging its U.S.-based manufacturing advantage.

sources.title: TrendForce Sees Tightening Advanced Packaging and 3nm Capacity as AI Competition Turns Into a Supply Chain Arms Race

stories.headline: Trump Calls Iran's Reply to Peace Plan 'Totally Unacceptable'; Brent Jumps 4% to $105

key_facts.fact: Iran sent its response to the latest US ceasefire proposal to Pakistani mediators on Sunday, May 10, saying negotiations should focus on permanently ending hostilities across the region
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has sent its response to the latest U.S. ceasefire proposal to Pakistani mediators and wants negotiations to focus on permanently ending the war, Iran's state-run media said Sunday.

key_facts.fact: President Trump called Iran's counterproposal 'totally unacceptable' Sunday hours after Tehran delivered it through Pakistani mediators
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump called Iran's response to the latest U.S. proposal to end the war 'totally unacceptable.'

key_facts.fact: Washington's 14-point plan requires Iran to end its nuclear programme for at least 12 years and open the Strait of Hormuz, while lifting decades-long sanctions; Iran demands war reparations, full sovereignty over the strait, an end to the US blockade and release of frozen assets
key_facts.excerpt: Washington floated a 14-point proposal earlier this week, which requires Iran to end its nuclear programme for at least 12 years and open the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global crude oil and gas passes. The US proposal includes lifting the decades-long sanctions.

key_facts.fact: A QatarEnergy-operated LNG carrier, al Kharaitiyat, was permitted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz Sunday and head for Pakistan's Port Qasim, the first Qatari LNG vessel through the strait since the war started February 28
key_facts.excerpt: But the QatarEnergy-operated carrier al Kharaitiyat passed safely through the strait and was heading for Pakistan's Port Qasim, according to data from shipping analytics firm Kpler, the first Qatari vessel carrying liquefied natural gas to cross the strait since the U.S. and Israel started the war on Feb. 28.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures climbed $4.16, or 4.11%, to $105.45 a barrel in Monday Asian trading; WTI rose $4.38, or 4.59%, to $99.80
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures climbed $4.16 or 4.11% to $105.45 a barrel at 0340 GMT. U.S. West Texas Intermediate was at $99.80 a barrel, up $4.38, or 4.59%.

key_facts.fact: Both Brent and WTI had recorded 6% weekly losses the prior week on hopes of an imminent deal that would reopen the strait; ING analysts now expect Brent to stay above $90 through 2026 and $80–85 into 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Last week, both contracts recorded 6% weekly losses on hopes for an imminent end to the 10-week-old conflict... They expected Brent to remain above $90 per barrel through 2026 and around $80 to $85 per barrel into 2027 as demand growth resumes and inventories are gradually rebuilt.

stories.headline: Trump-Xi Summit Set May 14-15 in Beijing; Iran, Taiwan, AI, Nuclear Arms on Agenda

key_facts.fact: US President Donald Trump will meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14 and 15, his first trip to China since 2017 and first leader-level US visit to Beijing in nearly a decade
key_facts.excerpt: Trump is scheduled to arrive in Beijing on Wednesday, ahead of talks set to take place Thursday and Friday. It will be his first trip to China since 2017.

key_facts.fact: US officials briefing reporters on May 10 said the agenda will span Iran, Taiwan, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons, with both sides weighing whether to extend a critical-minerals truce reached last October
key_facts.excerpt: U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to discuss Iran, Taiwan, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons as they weigh extending a critical minerals deal, according to U.S. officials previewing Trump's two-day visit to China this week.

key_facts.fact: China is expected to announce purchases of Boeing aircraft, US agricultural goods and energy, with proposals under discussion including 25 million metric tons of soybeans annually for three years and a potential deal for 500 Boeing 737 MAX jets
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. is pushing for significant Chinese purchases of poultry, beef, and energy products, alongside a multi-year commitment to buy 25 million metric tons of soybeans annually. A centerpiece of the discussions involves Boeing, which has been in prolonged talks with Beijing for a deal potentially including 500 737 MAX jets.

key_facts.fact: Iran is a flashpoint heading into the meeting: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has urged Beijing to help reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while China maintains that ending the war is Washington's responsibility
key_facts.excerpt: The Iran war presents a complex diplomatic hurdle. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has urged China to join efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though Beijing maintains that ending the conflict is Washington's responsibility.

key_facts.fact: Beijing 'is working backward from our midterm elections,' meaning major economic concessions are unlikely; the two sides are expected to set up a 'Board of Trade' mechanism to expand commerce in non-sensitive sectors
key_facts.excerpt: China may not offer breakthroughs when Trump meets Xi because Beijing is 'working backward from our midterm elections'

key_facts.excerpt: German robotics software company Sereact has raised a USD 110 million Series B round led by Headline, with participation from Bullhound Capital, Daphni, and Felix Capital.

key_facts.fact: Existing investors Air Street Capital, Creandum (which led the 2025 Series A), and Point Nine returned for the round.
key_facts.excerpt: Existing investors Air Street Capital, Creandum (lead of Sereact's 2025 Series A), and Point Nine all returned for this round.

key_facts.fact: The capital funds two priorities: scaling Cortex 2.0, Sereact's next-generation robotic-brain model for robots working in the physical world, and entering the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: The Series B round funds two priorities: scaling Cortex 2.0, the next generation of Sereact's robotic brain, and entering the United States.

key_facts.excerpt: Tessera Labs announced $60 million in oversubscribed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) to accelerate its mission of bringing AI-native automation to enterprise transformation.

key_facts.fact: a16z partner Seema Amble joined Tessera Labs' board of directors as part of the round.
key_facts.excerpt: Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) led the round, with Partner Seema Amble joining Tessera Labs's board of directors.
